notes.why: Rout 909 has no notes: each drum sounds from its trigger column (a 1 on a row hits it), at its level. Each becomes a note on Neo Drums' key for the voice (C2 kick, D2 snare, G2 B2 D3 toms, C#2 rim, D#2 clap, F#2 and A#2 hats, C#3 crash, D#3 ride), at velocity 127.

Neo Drums has no swing: the hits land on their rows as written (Rout 909 delays every other step by up to half a tick)

tolerance.why_not: Rout 909 plays samples of a TR-909; Neo Drums synthesises its voices: their spectra match within a few dB where each voice has most of its energy, not band for band. The level is matched and checked.

remarks: Neo Drums' defaults were voiced against the Rout 909's samples at its defaults (third octaves, pitch over time, decay); Volume +7.5 dB makes up the headroom Neo Drums keeps.
Rout 909's parameters are bare 0–63 scales: each was measured at 0, 16, 32, 48 and 63 (DrumsCalibration, ReBuzzTests) and laid on Neo Drums' units through those points.
Neo Drums' cowbell is left as it is: Rout 909 has none.
evidence: ReBuzzTests/DrumsCalibration.cs: each drum alone at its defaults and at 0, 16, 32, 48 and 63 of each scale, its level at 0, 64, 192 and 254 (peaks, the times to fall 20, 40 and 60 dB, centroids, pitch over time, third octaves)
